item: The allocator reading says what glibc did with the variable: the first of two entries, a plain decimal number, nothing under a preloaded malloc or an arena-limit tunable (the Opus read of #1304)
key_paths: src/monitoring/session_hwm.py; src/monitoring/soak_window.py; scripts/launch.sh; tests/test_malloc_arena_default.py; docs/CHANGES.md; docs/ledger/RULINGS_INDEX.md; docs/ledger/LESSONS.md
summary: The read of R114 (#1304, merged before it ended) ran glibc 2.39 itself with crafted environments and found that the allocator setting each session records could say the opposite of what the allocator did. A variable named twice reads as its FIRST value, which is the one glibc and os.environ apply (8 then 1 gives 8 arenas; the reading said capped at 1, and the test pinned that wrong order). A number counts only in the plain decimal form glibc reads the way a person does (leading blanks or tabs allowed; 4 followed by a space, 08, 010, 0x4, a non-ASCII digit and a 23-digit number are each not claimed, and read as not known). GLIBC_TUNABLES naming glibc.malloc.arena_max outranks the variable and reads as not known; a preloaded jemalloc, tcmalloc or mimalloc has no glibc arenas and reads as not capped; an empty starting environment is an env -i start and no longer falls back to os.environ; arena_cap names only a cap the process runs with. The soak window's memory-guard block now carries the setting when the guard's own state cannot be read (its fourth early return), the launcher's comment and the changelog no longer say freed memory stays in its own thread's arena, and a launcher test pins that an install file that unsets or empties the variable, or a caller that passes it empty, still gets the default. A new test starts a child through execve with the variable named twice and counts the arenas glibc kept (it skips where nothing creates per-thread arenas); the Windows lane's path comparison in the starting-block fake uses as_posix. Fifteen mutations of the reading, the launcher's order and the soak window are each caught. Lesson: LESSONS.md, A READING OF ANOTHER PROGRAM'S BEHAVIOUR IS TESTED BY RUNNING THAT PROGRAM, NOT BY AGREEING WITH THE CODE.
